Should a long-term investor take a minority stake in Liebherr – and if not, why not yet?

WHAT IT MEANS
The advantage is real – but it sits in the asset base, not yet in the margin.
For the investor the question is not whether the advantage exists, but whether it is turned into returns.

Overall assessment and investment perspective

What would have to change: three conditions for a reassessment

Check them on the 2026 statements – a new assessment only if all three are met. In 2025 none of them is.
1
Operating margin of at least 3.9 % (four-year average)
Status 2025
✗ 2.8 %
2
Free cash flow positive and, over time, covering distributions
Status 2025
✗ −€176 m
3
Information rights: audited statements and other operating expenses
Status 2025
✗ Not secured
REWARD
Resilient, diversified group · back to the 3.9 % average margin = +€157 m operating profit at 2025 revenue
RISK AND LIMITS
ROCE 3.5 % (pre-tax) vs. 7.70 % benchmark – needs a margin of ~6–8 % · minority stake: little influence, low payout, hard to sell
Even then: meeting the conditions triggers a new analysis, not a purchase – a minority stake in an unlisted group would only make sense at a discounted price.
Source: Report §5.3, §5.7 and chapter 8, Table 3; Excel workbook, sheets D3, D10 and D11; benchmark: Damodaran (2026a)
10
Conclusion

Financially strong.
Operationally challenged.

1
The balance sheet is strong – and stays strong
53.5 % equity ratio and 2.6× cash cover; still ≈ 50 % equity ratio in our depreciation sensitivity.
2
Returns and cash generation are too weak
2.8 % margin, 12.5–16.2 pp below Caterpillar in every year; free cash flow negative in 3 of 4 years.
3
The accounting sharpens the verdict
The measured effects point to a margin of 1.6–2.8 %, and key estimates cannot be verified from outside.
Not yet: the investor should see the turn in the figures before committing capital.

Backup · A | Business model

Environment: a modest recovery, but costs rise first

DESTEP scan
◂ INDEX
Economic
European construction equipment market +4.6 % in 2025, +2 to 2.5 % expected for 2026 – while Liebherr's construction and mining revenue fell 5.5 %.
Political
US tariffs cut Liebherr's North American crane revenue in 2025. Caterpillar expected a tariff impact of $2,600 m in 2026.
Social
Construction had 792 fatal accidents at work in the EU in 2023, 24.0 % of the total. Safety becomes a purchase criterion.
Technological
Autonomous and electrified machines. EU Regulation 2023/1230 covers autonomous functions from 20 January 2027.
Ecological
EU emission limits for non-road machinery and the target of at least 55 % net emission cuts by 2030 make low-emission machines a purchase criterion.
Demographic
Shortages of skilled workers and machine operators push costs up. Personnel expenses reached 28.6 % of revenue in 2025.
Source: Report §3.1.1; CECE (2026), Eurostat (2025), European Union (2023), Liebherr-International AG (2026), Caterpillar Inc. (2026)

Backup · A | Business model

Competitive forces squeeze the margin

Porter's five forces
◂ INDEX
New entrants
Moderate, rising
Chinese producers enter with cheaper, simplified machines. Mobile and crawler crane revenue fell 6.8 % in 2025.
Supplier power
Moderate, rising
Cost of materials is 52.7 % of revenue. Electrification shifts power to battery and electronics suppliers.
Buyer power
High, stable
Receivables rose 9.1 % against revenue growth of 1.0 % in 2025. About half of fleet owners may reconsider their brands by 2028.
Substitutes
Low to moderate, rising
Renting and automation change how much equipment is needed. The rental fleet took €305 m, 28.8 % of 2025 investment.
Rivalry
High, rising
The fixed cost of staying in the market rises. The operating margin fell from 4.6 % in 2024 to 2.8 % in 2025.
Investor lens Limited industry profit potential – consistent with the fall to 2.8 %
Source: Report §3.1.2, Table 1; ratings are the judgement of the report

Backup · B | Accounting analysis

Red-flag screen: reasons to ask, not proof

Nine tests over four years
◂ INDEX
Four red flags
  • Provision reversals: €143 m in 2025, 34.6 % of the operating result if credited within it
  • Receivables vs. revenue: receivables +9.1 % against revenue +1.0 % in 2025
  • Profit vs. tax: effective tax rate 99.2 %, 45.1 %, 58.2 % and 37.8 % (2022–2025), no reconciliation
  • Impairment: €55 m in 2023, six times the level of the other years
Clean or not testable
  • Clean: no off-balance-sheet arrangements disclosed · same auditor (Ernst & Young), no qualified opinion · no change of policy or estimate
  • Not testable: related party transactions (no note in four years) · large year-end adjustments (no interim figures)

Why 3.9 % is only a trigger, not a target

Condition 1 of the reassessment
◂ INDEX
3.9 %
Average operating margin 2022–2025 (3.86 %)
+€157 m
Operating profit at 2025 revenue (€14,772 m)
3.5 %
ROCE before tax 2025 vs. 7.70 % after-tax benchmark
6–8 %
Operating margin needed to earn the benchmark
What the trigger means
  • A return to 3.9 % is the first realistic sign of recovery – Liebherr has earned it on average
  • It is a test, not a target return
  • Each margin point is worth €148 m
Why it is not enough
  • Even in 2024, at a 4.6 % margin, ROCE was only 5.9 % before tax – below the 7.70 % benchmark
  • The benchmark is the US machinery industry, not Liebherr's own cost of capital
  • A margin recovery alone does not prove an adequate return
Source: Report §5.3 and §5.7, chapter 8; Excel workbook, sheets D3 and D10; Damodaran (2026a)

Backup · D | Recommendation

Risks, limits and when to drop the case

What could still go wrong – and the alternative for a cautious investor
◂ INDEX
Demand
Construction and mining revenue −5.5 % in 2025; no significant upswing expected before 2027
Costs
US tariffs and the cost of autonomous and electrified machines press on the margin
Information
The largest cost increase of 2025 cannot be explained from the summary statements
Valuation
Not assessed in the report – price and contract rights decide the case
Alternative for a risk-averse investor
Equity is unsuitable: low payout, shares not traded. A loan may fit better, as equity of 53.5 % limits the default risk – but pricing, maturity, collateral and covenants are not disclosed.
Drop trigger
If the margin stays near 2.8 % in 2026 and the net financial position turns negative, the investor should drop the case rather than wait for 2027. A recovery should not rest on large provision releases.
Source: Report §5.5, §5.7, §6.1 and chapter 8

Backup · E | Likely questions

Why not invest now?

Likely questions (1/2)
◂ INDEX
Q
Why not invest now?
Neither financial condition was met in 2025: the margin of 2.8 % is below its four-year average of 3.9 %, and free cash flow was −€176 m. The answer is not yet, rather than no.
Q
Why is 3.9 % the first test?
It is the average Liebherr earned from 2022 to 2025 – a realistic first sign of recovery. At 2025 revenue it adds €157 m of operating profit. A trigger, not a target return.
Q
Is the LIFO to FIFO adjustment fair?
IAS 2 does not permit LIFO, so FIFO puts both groups on one basis. Caterpillar's LIFO reserve of $4,305 m lifts its margin only from 16.50 % to 17.15 % – the gap stays large.
Source: Report chapters 4 to 8; Excel workbook, sheets C1, D3 and D10
28
Backup · E | Likely questions

What the balance sheet cannot fix

Likely questions (2/2)
◂ INDEX
Q
What do the red flags mean?
They are reasons to ask, not proof of manipulation. Four flags are raised, three tests are clean and two cannot be run on the published statements – that is why information rights come first.
Q
Why is ROCE so low?
ROCE is 3.5 % before tax against a 7.70 % after-tax benchmark: the margin is only 2.8 %, and inventories of 42.9 % of revenue and a cash cycle 77 days longer than Caterpillar's tie up capital.
Q
Why is a strong balance sheet not a return?
An equity ratio of 53.5 % and a net financial position of €249 m limit the risk, but do not earn the cost of capital. They would cover a shortfall like 2025 (−€232 m) for about 1.1 years.
Source: Report chapters 4 to 8; Excel workbook, sheets C1, D3 and D10
